From: Gomez, Pedro J. <Pedro.J.Gomez@espn.com>
Sent: Tuesday, November 25, 2014 6:33 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: My info 
 
Anthony,
Really great to meet and I love the enthusiasm you're showing for your new gig. That's such a big part of being successful as a ball writer.
A couple of things that really helped me as a beat writer, things that were passed down to me:

1. Remember, you're a beat writer for the Tigers. That means you basically have 25 relationships with 25 players. It's important for you to maintain that attitude. I always thought it was important to simply say, "hey" to guys at least every few days, if not every day. It just helps you maintain a relationship. Also, if a player makes a great play, even if it's just a really solid baseball play that you won't write about, be sure you acknowledge that to him. It just shows that you're paying attention, which will earn you respect.
2. Maintain a relationship with every coach. Those guys are invaluable when it comes to giving you background on what's going on.

3. Every single series, be sure you go introduce yourself to the opposing manager and GM. After a while, they'll know who you are and you never know when those guys can help you with a story. Be sure you walk through the opposing clubhouse and chat with a few players with some regularity. It will help down the road.

4. Remember, you're writing for your audience, not the Tigers. If you don't get yelled at every once in a while, then you're probably not doing your job correctly. If Dombrowski, Ausmus or players don't call you out once in a while, ask yourself why?

It's going to take time for you to truly know what's going on with the club. Even if you're there every day, it takes time -- I was told three seasons and it wound up being accurate -- to build sources and truly have a grasp. Gage has been there forever and it won't be easy. But you'll be great.

My contact info is listed below. Call on me for whatever advice I might be able to help with. 
All the best,
Pedro

Pedro Gomez
